sources.title: B. H. Bowditch, Notes on locally CAT(1) spaces (Aberdeen preprint, 27 scanned sheets, two printed pages per sheet)
sources.locator: §§2–3.4, printed pp. 13–32 of the scanned preprint: local geodesics and injectivity radius (2.16); loop classes, closed local geodesics and short-loop homotopy (3.1.4–3.1.7); the product model (3.2.1); midpoint polygons and the energy functional (3.3.1–3.3.6); the finite comparison disk, radius/quadrilateral estimates and the quantitative decrement (3.3.8–3.3.15); the shrinkable-loop conclusions (3.4). §§3.5–3.7 and the remaining printed pages were not read.

contents.name: 3.1.6–3.1.7: midpoint-iteration limit classes; every loop shorter than the minimal embedded-circle length m is shrinkable, and the minimal embedded circle is a shortest nonshrinkable loop
3.2.1: the product model S²×S² and its curvature bound (the printed 'curvature ≤ −1' is a typo for ≤ 1)
3.3.1–3.3.4: the midpoint operation; mesh, length and energy do not increase, with the equality case for constant polygons and for equally spaced vertices of a closed local geodesic
3.3.8–3.3.15: the quantitative energy decrement, the comparison disk, the radius and quadrilateral estimates, and the closedness of the zero-limit class
3.4: passage between rectifiable loops and polygons by chord subdivision and local interpolation, with nonincreasing length
§§3.5–3.7 and the remaining printed pages: applications to particular complexes and curve-shortening flows
contents.reason: These later sections concern applications to particular complexes and flows; this pair needs only the general short-loop class and quantitative energy theory of §§2–3.4, which is already supplied by the short-loop page.

contents.name: §3.1.6–3.1.7, printed pp. 19–20: shorter loops are shrinkable and the sub-2π minimum embedded circle is attained as a shortest nonshrinkable loop; consumed provisionally through the escalated Bowditch supplier

sources.title: Martin R. Bridson and André Haefliger, Metric Spaces of Non-Positive Curvature (Springer Grundlehren 319, 1999; author-hosted PDF)
sources.locator: Chapter II.5.1–II.5.4 read in full from the extracted text of the author-hosted PDF (printed pp. 206–207: the link condition, Gromov's Theorem 5.2 with its use of I.7.39 and Berestovskii's theorem III.3.14, and Theorem 5.4 including the κ>0 short-circle form). II.1.4 and II.4.9–II.4.16 are recorded through the commissioned geometric source report's readings of the same file. The rest of the book was not read for this batch.

contents.name: II.5.1–II.5.2 with I.7.39 and II.3.14: the link condition; an M_κ-polyhedral complex with finitely many shapes has curvature ≤ κ if and only if every vertex link is CAT(1), via the local model at a vertex as a neighbourhood of the cone point in C_κ(Lk(v,K)) and Berestovskii's cone theorem
II.5.4: for κ>0, CAT(κ) is equivalent to the link condition together with the absence of isometrically embedded circles of length < 2π/√κ
III.3.14: the Euclidean cone over a CAT(1) space is CAT(0), and conversely (Berestovskii's theorem)
II.4.9–II.4.16: injectivity radius, the compact systole theorem and the minimum isometrically embedded circle of length 2·injrad(X)
II.1.4: unique geodesics for distances below D_κ, local geodesics of length ≤ D_κ are geodesics, and convex balls of radius < D_κ/2
II.1.1–II.1.8: model spaces, the hinge/cosine comparison and monotonicity of the model spaces in κ
The remainder of the book (Chapters I.1–I.6, II.6–II.12, Chapter III)
contents.reason: The pair consumes only the CAT(κ) comparison, cone, link-criterion and systole material of I.3, II.1, II.3–II.5; the remaining chapters treat complexes of groups, boundaries and applications not stated or used by any item.

sources.title: Michael W. Davis, The Geometry and Topology of Coxeter Groups (first-edition author manuscript, 2007-2008)
sources.locator: §7.1, printed pp. 123–124 (spherical subsets and the combinatorial nerve), and §12.1, Lemma 12.1.1 and §12.3, Lemma 12.3.1, printed pp. 231–235 (the natural piecewise-spherical structure, cosine matrices, edge lengths and positive-definite face test), read directly for this item. Appendix I.2.6–I.2.19, printed pp. 502–507, remains recorded through the commissioned source report; the rest of the book was not read for this batch. Appendix I.7.4, printed pp. 521–522, was re-read directly for item lem-cg-minimum-nonshrinkable-loop-and-radial-vertex-insertion: it gives a proof sketch of constant-length radial replacement and maximal-vertex reduction, but leaves the constant-length homotopy as "clear" rather than constructing its uniform-plus-length continuity.

contents.name: I.2.17–I.2.18: the cone on a CAT(1) space is CAT(0), with its geodesic radial structure
I.2.8 and I.2.15: the κ>0 criterion and the hinged quadratic inequality
I.2.16: local geodesics are geodesics up to D_κ
§7.1; §12.1, Lemma 12.1.1; §12.3, Lemma 12.3.1: the nerve on spherical subsets, its induced piecewise-spherical link metric, the Coxeter cosine matrix, and edge lengths π−π/m
Chapter 7.4–7.5, Chapter 13 and the hyperbolic and arithmetic applications of the Davis complex
contents.reason: Those chapters concern the hyperbolic criterion, Davis complex topology beyond the nerve metric and applications not stated or used by any item of this pair; the pair stops at the girth bound.

contents.name: Appendix I.7.4, printed pp. 521–522: proof sketch for radial replacement of a minimum short loop and the maximum-vertex reduction

sources.title: G. Moussong, Hyperbolic Coxeter groups, PhD thesis (Ohio State University 1988), McCammond transcription
sources.locator: Chapter 1, §§4–5 (almost-negative matrices and the girth of a finite S-complex); Chapter 2, §7, printed pp. 15–16, read directly for this item (N(A) as the union of spherical simplices indexed by positive-definite principal submatrices with compatible faces); §9 (intrinsic metric) and §10, printed pp. 24–25, including Proposition 10.1 and Corollary 10.2, from the earlier extracted-text reading. The original scan and remaining sections were not read here. For item lem-cg-minimum-nonshrinkable-loop-and-radial-vertex-insertion, Chapter 1, §5, Lemma 5.4 (printed pp. 11–12) and Chapter 2, §9, Lemma 9.8 (printed pp. 22–23) were re-read directly; Lemma 9.8 proves its radial-projection seam argument by induction, while its hypotheses must still be matched to the consumer excursion.

contents.name: Chapter 2, §7: the nerve N(A) is the union of spherical cells for positive-definite principal submatrices, glued by their face maps
Proposition 10.1: the girth of the nerve N(A) of an almost negative matrix is at least 2π
Corollary 10.2: the girth of lk(B, N(A)) is at least 2π for every simplex B of N(A)

Chapter 1, §5, Lemma 5.4 and Chapter 2, §9, Lemma 9.8: cone geodesics and the inductive radial-projection seam argument; relevant to the open excursion step but not yet transplanted as a complete consumer proof
Lemma 9.11 (the star-avoiding excursion implication used in the case analysis of Proposition 10.1)
contents.reason: Recorded as a source defect: Moeller (arXiv:2205.07791) exhibits counterexamples to its general form. The proof of this page replaces the step by the direct three-edge argument of thm-cg-large-metric-flag-short-loop-radial-contradiction and never consumes Lemma 9.11, so no item is built on it.

contents.name: Chapters 3–4 (the hyperbolic criterion and its strictness analysis) and the appendices
contents.reason: The hyperbolic characterization of Coxeter groups is not stated or used by any item of this pair; the pair proves the CAT(1)/girth part only, and the hyperbolic case is exactly where the repaired gap lies.

sources.title: Ruth Charney and Michael W. Davis, The Euler characteristic of a nonpositively curved, piecewise Euclidean manifold, Pacific J. Math. 171 (1995), 117–142
sources.locator: §§1–3 read in the publisher PDF: 1.1–1.3 (piecewise Euclidean and spherical cell complexes, links and the geodesic metric), 2.1–2.4.1 (large piecewise spherical spaces, cosine matrices, all-right and size > π/2 simplices and their links), 2.7–2.10 (flag complexes, Gromov's Lemma, metric flag complexes, Moussong's Lemma), 3.4.2 and 3.6.3 (the invariant κ and joins). Sections 4–7 (conjectures and partial results) were not read.

contents.name: §2.3.2: a positive-definite cosine matrix determines a spherical simplex, unique up to isometry
2.9: the definition of a metric flag complex: a simplicial complex such that every set of vertices spanning a complete graph and having positive-definite cosine matrix spans a simplex
2.10: Moussong's Lemma — a piecewise spherical simplicial cell complex with simplices of size > π/2 is large (unique geodesics below π) if and only if it is a metric flag complex
2.4.1: the link of a face of a simplex of size > π/2 again has size > π/2
2.1.1 and 2.7–2.8: large links; Gromov's Lemma (an all-right piecewise spherical simplicial complex is large if and only if it is a flag complex)
2.3.2: existence and uniqueness, up to isometry, of a spherical simplex with a prescribed positive-definite cosine matrix
3.6.3: the orthogonal join of piecewise spherical complexes and the join formula for κ
Sections 4–7: the Hopf-type conjectures A–D and the partial results proved for them
contents.reason: The conjectures and their evidence concern Euler-characteristic signs of nonpositively curved manifolds and have no bearing on the CAT(1) metric-flag theorem, its girth bound or the Coxeter nerve.

sources.title: Philip Moeller, A note on almost negative matrices and Gromov-hyperbolic Coxeter groups, arXiv:2205.07791 (2023)
sources.locator: §§1–3 read in the arXiv PDF; §2, printed pp. 3–5, read directly for this item (almost-negative Coxeter cosine matrix, spherical nerve cells for positive-definite principal submatrices, face gluing, and the Moussong metric on the Davis complex); §2 Lemma 2.1 for links; §3 through Theorem 3.2, Propositions 3.3–3.4, Lemma 3.7 and the discussion of the gap in Moussong’s Lemmas 9.5, 9.7 and 9.11. §4 was not read. For item lem-cg-minimum-nonshrinkable-loop-and-radial-vertex-insertion, §3, Lemma 3.10 and its explicit 4×4 counterexample to Moussong Lemma 9.11 were re-read directly; this is warning context only and not proof support.

contents.name: §2: the Coxeter cosine matrix is almost negative, its positive-definite principal submatrices form a spherical nerve complex, and the Davis complex carries the corresponding Moussong metric
§2, Lemma 2.1: the link of a simplex B_I in N(A) is isometric to the nerve of the link matrix lk(I,A), and link matrices are again almost negative
§3, Theorem 3.2: an M_κ-polyhedral complex with finitely many shapes is locally CAT(κ) if and only if the link of every vertex is CAT(1)
§3, Proposition 3.3: the nerve complex of an almost negative matrix is CAT(1) if and only if its girth and the girths of all its links are at least 2π
§3, Proposition 3.4 ([Moussong, Corollary 10.2]): for a Coxeter system with cosine matrix A one has girth(N(A)) ≥ 2π and girth(N(lk(I,A))) ≥ 2π for all positive-definite A_I
§3, Proposition A with Lemma 3.7 and Lemma B: the exact failure of Moussong's Lemmas 9.5, 9.7 and 9.11 in the presence of zero rows in link matrices, and the splitting repair
contents.reason: This is a defect and repair record for the Gromov-hyperbolic criterion, which this pair does not state; it is cited in the page's source note so that no future consumer treats the disputed step as available.

contents.name: §4 and Theorem C: the Gromov-hyperbolic characterization of Coxeter groups via the absence of Z² subgroups
contents.reason: The hyperbolic characterization needs the strict girth analysis on spherical links and the extended-affine exclusions; the pair proves only the CAT(1) girth bound and deliberately makes no hyperbolicity claim.
